newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares record run seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares record run seen continuing.

text.p: The Brussels bourse's record breaking run is intact despite late pressure on prices on Monday that left the leading stock index little changed, analysts said.

"The dollar is firmer, bond yields are lower...nothing has fundamentally changed," Gert De Mesure of Antwerp's Bank Delen said, noting buying in banks and holdings ahead of the dividend season that starts on Friday.
Late selling knocked around five points off the Bel-20 leading stock index. But the index still ended 1.04 points up at a new closing high of 2,254.87 points.
Volume was thin due to a market holiday in London.

Among industrials, cement maker CBR gained 10 francs to 3,575 francs. One dealer attributed interest in the stock to speculation ahead of the company's annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday, where a forecast on 1997 earnings is likely. However, shipping company CMB, which also holds its AGM on Wednesday, slipped 15 francs to 2,560 francs.

Fast food retailer Quick gained ground late, ending up 50 francs at 1,800 francs, on news of an upgrade to hold from sell by brokerage BBL/Vermeulen-Raemdonck. A trader at another house also estimated the stock was a hold. "It could even be a buy if you are ready to wait a long time," he added.
Financials and holdings, offering high dividend yields, were still the main focus of attention, along with selected cyclical issues, offering profit growth, dealers said.
Bank Kredietbank, which pays a 235 franc net dividend on Friday, added 100 francs to 14,275 francs.
Insurer Royale Belge, which is due to pay a 360 franc gross dividend next month and is the subject of merger speculation, added 80 francs to 9,350 francs.
Holding Societe Generale de Belgique rose 35 francs to 3,250 francs. SGB unit Finoutremer, which is offering a 155 franc dividend, added 80 francs to 4,400.
